A panel of A-I specialists that would look at the same eye, argue, and reach a verdict together.

beats.series_slot: BODY ¶1 — THE TAUGHT CONCEPT: vision-language models
beats.narration_text: To build it, we used a new kind of model: a vision-language model. A plain classifier turns an image into a silent list of numbers — powerful, but it can't tell you why. A vision-language model is trained on images and text together, so it can look at a scan, read the measurements, and reason in words — the way a clinician thinks aloud. That difference matters in medicine, where a number without a reason is very hard to act on, and impossible to audit.

props.caption: Conceptual. No performance claim is made in this episode.

beats.narration_text: Then we did something more interesting than using one. We built three, each with a different expertise — a structural specialist that read the O-C-T nerve map, a functional specialist that read the visual-field test, and a director who weighed them both. And we had them deliberate over three rounds: each specialist gives its read, then sees the others' opinions, reconsiders, and revises — before the director delivers the final call.

props.sparkLine: Three reads, three rounds, one verdict.
roles: structural specialist — reads the OCT nerve map
functional specialist — reads the visual field
director — weighs both and calls it
three rounds: read → see the others → revise
props.caption: Our design. Proposed and under evaluation — not a benchmarked result.

beats.narration_text: Why a council instead of a single model? Because that's how hard medical decisions actually get made — a tumour board, a panel, specialists challenging each other until the truth surfaces. The research on multi-agent A-I backs the intuition: models that critique each other can catch errors a lone model sails right past. A lone model has one blind spot and no way to see it. Three models with different remits have to make their disagreement explicit before they can resolve it.

props.sparkLine: Models that critique each other catch more.
props.caption: Conceptual — the argument for deliberation, not a measured result.

beats.narration_text: We ran it on the flagged, uncertain cases — the exact eyes the classifier struggled with. And the early results were striking. Genuinely, excitingly striking. Which, in research, is precisely the moment you should get nervous.

beats.narration_text: A Council of Specialists. We were proud enough to submit it for peer review. And that's when an expert asked the one question we hadn't. Next time.
